      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "Based on the assessment referred to in paragraph 2, and in coordination with the Joint Oversight Network (JON) referred to in Article 34(1), the Lead Overseer shall adopt a clear, detailed and reasoned individual oversight plan describing the annual oversight objectives and the main oversight actions planned for each critical ICT third-party service provider. That plan shall be communicated yearly to the critical ICT third-party service provider.",
          "source_line_start": 6718,
          "source_line_end": 6718
        },
        {
          "sequence": 2,
          "text": "Prior to the adoption of the oversight plan, the Lead Overseer shall communicate the draft oversight plan to the critical ICT third-party service provider.",
          "source_line_start": 6719,
          "source_line_end": 6719
        },
        {
          "sequence": 3,
          "text": "Upon receipt of the draft oversight plan, the critical ICT third-party service provider may submit a reasoned statement within 15 calendar days evidencing the expected impact on customers which are entities falling outside of the scope of this Regulation and where appropriate, formulating solutions to mitigate risks.",
          "source_line_start": 6720,
          "source_line_end": 6720
        }
      ],
      "akn4eu_article_type_uri": "http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/resource-type/ART",
      "canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art33-Para4",
      "text_sha256": "5db9beb4b17c1084ec61f6673c7fbc7fd6539d4a29452e65bb4b23f615bf9c7b"
    },
    {
      "id": "article-Art33-Para5",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 33,
      "paragraph_number": "5",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
      "akn4eu_article_kind": "regular",
      "akn4eu_heading": "Tasks of the Lead Overseer",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "Once the annual oversight plans referred to in paragraph 4 have been adopted and notified to the critical ICT third-party service providers, competent authorities may take measures concerning such critical ICT third-party service providers only in agreement with the Lead Overseer.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art33-Para5__article-Art33-Para4__depends_on",
          "source": "article-Art33-Para5",
          "target": "article-Art33-Para4",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art33-Para5 -> article-Art33-Para4: Article 33(5)'s limit on competent-authority measures starts only after the oversight plan under Article 33(4) has been adopted and notified.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art33-Para5",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art33-Para4"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "recital-93__article-Art33-Para5__concretizes",
          "source": "recital-93",
          "target": "article-Art33-Para5",
          "source_type": "recital",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "concretizes",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "The bar in recital-93 on separate competent-authority monitoring of critical providers absent Lead Overseer agreement is stated operatively in article-Art33-Para5.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/recital-93",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art33-Para5"
        }
      ],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "Once the annual oversight plans referred to in paragraph 4 have been adopted and notified to the critical ICT third-party service providers, competent authorities may take measures concerning such critical ICT third-party service providers only in agreement with the Lead Overseer.",
          "source_line_start": 6723,
          "source_line_end": 6723
        }
      ],

    {

        "Section II"

          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art31-Para1"
        },
        {

        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "To ensure a consistent approach to oversight activities and with a view to enabling coordinated general oversight strategies and cohesive operational approaches and work methodologies, the three Lead Overseers appointed in accordance with Article 31(1), point (b), shall set up a JON to coordinate among themselves in the preparatory stages and to coordinate the conduct of oversight activities over their respective overseen critical ICT third-party service providers, as well as in the course of any action that may be needed pursuant to Article 42.",

    {
      "id": "article-Art34-Para2",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 34,
      "paragraph_number": "2",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
      "akn4eu_article_kind": "regular",
      "akn4eu_heading": "Operational coordination between Lead Overseers",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "For the purposes of paragraph 1, the Lead Overseers shall draw up a common oversight protocol specifying the detailed procedures to be followed for carrying out the day-to-day coordination and for ensuring swift exchanges and reactions. The protocol shall be periodically revised to reflect operational needs, in particular the evolution of practical oversight arrangements.",

          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art34-Para2 -> article-Art34-Para1: Article 34(2) requires the Lead Overseers to adopt the common protocol needed to carry out the JON coordination established in Article 34(1).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art34-Para2",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art34-Para1"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [

The protocol shall be periodically revised to reflect operational needs, in particular the evolution of practical oversight arrangements.",
          "source_line_start": 6735,

    {
      "id": "article-Art34-Para3",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 34,
      "paragraph_number": "3",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
      "akn4eu_article_kind": "regular",
      "akn4eu_heading": "Operational coordination between Lead Overseers",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "The Lead Overseers may, on an ad-hoc basis, call on the ECB and ENISA to provide technical advice, share hands-on experience or join specific coordination meetings of the JON.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art34-Para3__article-Art34-Para1__depends_on",
          "source": "article-Art34-Para3",
          "target": "article-Art34-Para1",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art34-Para3 -> article-Art34-Para1: the ad hoc ECB/ENISA advice and participation authorised by Article 34(3) concerns coordination meetings of the JON established and assigned its coordination role in Article 34(1).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art34-Para3",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art34-Para1"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "The Lead Overseers may, on an ad-hoc basis, call on the ECB and ENISA to provide technical advice, share hands-on experience or join specific coordination meetings of the JON.",
          "source_line_start": 6738,
          "source_line_end": 6738
        }
      ],
      "akn4eu_article_type_uri": "http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/resource-type/ART",

    {
      "id": "article-Art35-Para1",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 35,
      "paragraph_number": "1",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
      "akn4eu_article_kind": "regular",
      "akn4eu_heading": "Powers of the Lead Overseer",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(a)",
          "text": "to request all relevant information and documentation in accordance with Article 37;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(a)",
          "source_line_start": 6754,
          "source_line_end": 6757
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(b)",
          "text": "to conduct general investigations and inspections in accordance with Articles 38 and 39, respectively;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(b)",
          "source_line_start": 6768,
          "source_line_end": 6771
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(c)",
          "text": "to request, after the completion of the oversight activities, reports specifying the actions that have been taken or the remedies that have been implemented by the critical ICT third-party service providers in relation to the recommendations referred to in point (d) of this paragraph;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(c)",
          "source_line_start": 6782,
          "source_line_end": 6785
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(d)",
          "text": "to issue recommendations on the areas referred to in Article 33(3), in particular concerning the following: For the purpose of point (iv) of this point, ICT third-party service providers shall, using the template referred to in Article 41(1), point (b), transmit the information regarding subcontracting to the Lead Overseer.",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(d)",
          "source_line_start": 6796,
          "source_line_end": 6898
        },
        {
          "type": "subpoint",
          "marker": "(i)",
          "text": "the use of specific ICT security and quality requirements or processes, in particular in relation to the roll-out of patches, updates, encryption and other security measures which the Lead Overseer deems relevant for ensuring the ICT security of services provided to financial entities;",
          "depth": 2,
          "parent_marker": "(d)",
          "path": "(d)(i)",
          "source_line_start": 6806,
          "source_line_end": 6809
        },
        {
          "type": "subpoint",
          "marker": "(ii)",
          "text": "the use of conditions and terms, including their technical implementation, under which the critical ICT third-party service providers provide ICT services to financial entities, which the Lead Overseer deems relevant for preventing the generation of single points of failure, the amplification thereof, or for minimising the possible systemic impact across the Union’s financial sector in the event of ICT concentration risk;",
          "depth": 2,
          "parent_marker": "(d)",
          "path": "(d)(ii)",
          "source_line_start": 6820,
          "source_line_end": 6823
        },
        {
          "type": "subpoint",
          "marker": "(iii)",
          "text": "any planned subcontracting, where the Lead Overseer deems that further subcontracting, including subcontracting arrangements which the critical ICT third-party service providers plan to enter into with ICT third-party service providers or with ICT subcontractors established in a third country, may trigger risks for the provision of services by the financial entity, or risks to the financial stability, based on the examination of the information gathered in accordance with Articles 37 and 38;",
          "depth": 2,
          "parent_marker": "(d)",
          "path": "(d)(iii)",
          "source_line_start": 6834,
          "source_line_end": 6837
        },
        {
          "type": "subpoint",
          "marker": "(iv)",
          "text": "refraining from entering into a further subcontracting arrangement, where the following cumulative conditions are met:",
          "depth": 2,
          "parent_marker": "(d)",
          "path": "(d)(iv)",
          "source_line_start": 6848,
          "source_line_end": 6851
        },
        {
          "type": "subpoint",
          "marker": "—",
          "text": "the envisaged subcontractor is an ICT third-party service provider or an ICT subcontractor established in a third country;",
          "depth": 3,
          "parent_marker": "(iv)",
          "path": "(d)(iv)—",
          "source_line_start": 6858,
          "source_line_end": 6861
        },
        {
          "type": "subpoint",
          "marker": "—",
          "text": "the subcontracting concerns critical or important functions of the financial entity; and",
          "depth": 3,
          "parent_marker": "(iv)",
          "path": "(d)(iv)—",
          "source_line_start": 6872,
          "source_line_end": 6875
        },
        {
          "type": "subpoint",
          "marker": "—",
          "text": "the Lead Overseer deems that the use of such subcontracting poses a clear and serious risk to the financial stability of the Union or to financial entities, including to the ability of financial entities to comply with supervisory requirements.",
          "depth": 3,
          "parent_marker": "(iv)",
          "path": "(d)(iv)—",
          "source_line_start": 6886,
          "source_line_end": 6889
        }
      ],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "For the purposes of carrying out the duties laid down in this Section, the Lead Overseer shall have the following powers in respect of the critical ICT third-party service providers: (a) to request all relevant information and documentation in accordance with Article 37; (b) to conduct general investigations and inspections in accordance with Articles 38 and 39, respectively; (c) to request, after the completion of the oversight activities, reports specifying the actions that have been taken or the remedies that have been implemented by the critical ICT third-party service providers in relation to the recommendations referred to in point (d) of this paragraph; (d) to issue recommendations on the areas referred to in Article 33(3), in particular concerning the following: (i) the use of specific ICT security and quality requirements or processes, in particular in relation to the roll-out of patches, updates, encryption and other security measures which the Lead Overseer deems relevant for ensuring the ICT security of services provided to financial entities; (ii) the use of conditions and terms, including their technical implementation, under which the critical ICT third-party service providers provide ICT services to financial entities, which the Lead Overseer deems relevant for preventing the generation of single points of failure, the amplification thereof, or for minimising the possible systemic impact across the Union’s financial sector in the event of ICT concentration risk; (iii) any planned subcontracting, where the Lead Overseer deems that further subcontracting, including subcontracting arrangements which the critical ICT third-party service providers plan to enter into with ICT third-party service providers or with ICT subcontractors established in a third country, may trigger risks for the provision of services by the financial entity, or risks to the financial stability, based on the examination of the information gathered in accordance with Articles 37 and 38; (iv) refraining from entering into a further subcontracting arrangement, where the following cumulative conditions are met: — the envisaged subcontractor is an ICT third-party service provider or an ICT subcontractor established in a third country; — the subcontracting concerns critical or important functions of the financial entity; and — the Lead Overseer deems that the use of such subcontracting poses a clear and serious risk to the financial stability of the Union or to financial entities, including to the ability of financial entities to comply with supervisory requirements. For the purpose of point (iv) of this point, ICT third-party service providers shall, using the template referred to in Article 41(1), point (b), transmit the information regarding subcontracting to the Lead Overseer.",

          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "For the purposes of carrying out the duties laid down in this Section, the Lead Overseer shall have the following powers in respect of the critical ICT third-party service providers:",

          "source_line_end": 6747
        }

          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(a)",
          "text": "ensure regular coordination within the JON, and in particular shall seek consistent approaches, as appropriate, with regard to the oversight of critical ICT third-party service providers;",

          "source_line_start": 6912,

          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(b)",
          "text": "take due account of the framework established by Directive (EU) 2022/2555 and, where necessary, consult the relevant competent authorities designated or established in accordance with that Directive, in order to avoid duplication of technical and organisational measures that might apply to critical ICT third-party service providers pursuant to that Directive;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,

          "source_line_start": 6926,
          "source_line_end": 6929
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(c)",
          "text": "seek to minimise, to the extent possible, the risk of disruption to services provided by critical ICT third-party service providers to customers that are entities falling outside the scope of this Regulation.",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(c)",
          "source_line_start": 6940,
          "source_line_end": 6943
        }
      ],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "When exercising the powers referred to in this Article, the Lead Overseer shall: (a) ensure regular coordination within the JON, and in particular shall seek consistent approaches, as appropriate, with regard to the oversight of critical ICT third-party service providers; (b) take due account of the framework established by Directive (EU) 2022/2555 and, where necessary, consult the relevant competent authorities designated or established in accordance with that Directive, in order to avoid duplication of technical and organisational measures that might apply to critical ICT third-party service providers pursuant to that Directive; (c) seek to minimise, to the extent possible, the risk of disruption to services provided by critical ICT third-party service providers to customers that are entities falling outside the scope of this Regulation.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art35-Para2__article-Art34-Para1__depends_on",
          "source": "article-Art35-Para2",
          "target": "article-Art34-Para1",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art35-Para2 -> article-Art34-Para1: the obligation to coordinate regularly within the JON when exercising oversight powers depends on the JON structure and coordination mandate established by Article 34(1).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para2",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art34-Para1"
        },
        {

          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para1"
        }
      ],

      "text": "The Lead Overseer shall consult the Oversight Forum before exercising the powers referred to in paragraph 1.           "text": "Before issuing recommendations in accordance with paragraph 1, point (d), the Lead Overseer shall give the opportunity to the ICT third-party service provider to provide, within 30 calendar days, relevant information evidencing the expected impact on customers that are entities falling outside the scope of this Regulation and, where appropriate, formulating solutions to mitigate risks.",
          "source_line_start": 6951,
          "source_line_end": 6951
        }

      "type": "article_paragraph",

      "paragraph_number": "7",

      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "The periodic penalty payment referred to in paragraph 6 shall be imposed on a daily basis until compliance is achieved and for no more than a period of six months following the notification of the decision to impose a periodic penalty payment to the critical ICT third-party service provider.",
      "outbound_relations": [

          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art35-Para7 -> article-Art35-Para6: Article 35(7) fixes the daily accrual and six-month duration of the periodic penalty first authorised by Article 35(6).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para7",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para6"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {

          "text": "The periodic penalty payment referred to in paragraph 6 shall be imposed on a daily basis until compliance is achieved and for no more than a period of six months following the notification of the decision to impose a periodic penalty payment to the critical ICT third-party service provider.",
          "source_line_start": 6963,
          "source_line_end": 6963
        }

    {
      "id": "article-Art35-Para8",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 35,
      "paragraph_number": "8",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
      "akn4eu_article_kind": "regular",
      "akn4eu_heading": "Powers of the Lead Overseer",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(a)",
          "text": "the gravity and the duration of non-compliance;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(a)",
          "source_line_start": 6973,
          "source_line_end": 6976
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(b)",
          "text": "whether non-compliance has been committed intentionally or negligently;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(b)",
          "source_line_start": 6987,
          "source_line_end": 6990
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(c)",
          "text": "the level of cooperation of the ICT third-party service provider with the Lead Overseer.",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(c)",
          "source_line_start": 7001,
          "source_line_end": 7004
        }
      ],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "The amount of the periodic penalty payment, calculated from the date stipulated in the decision imposing the periodic penalty payment, shall be up to 1 % of the average daily worldwide turnover of the critical ICT third-party service provider in the preceding business year. When determining the amount of the penalty payment, the Lead Overseer shall take into account the following criteria regarding non-compliance with the measures referred to in paragraph 6: (a) the gravity and the duration of non-compliance; (b) whether non-compliance has been committed intentionally or negligently; (c) the level of cooperation of the ICT third-party service provider with the Lead Overseer. For the purposes of the first subparagraph, in order to ensure a consistent approach, the Lead Overseer shall engage in consultation within the JON.",

          "target": "article-Art34-Para1",

          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art35-Para8 -> article-Art34-Para1: consultation within the JON to ensure consistent calibration of periodic penalties depends on the JON coordination mechanism established by Article 34(1).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para8",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art34-Para1"
        },

    {
      "id": "article-Art35-Para9",
      "type": "article_paragraph",

      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "Penalty payments shall be of an administrative nature and shall be enforceable. Enforcement shall be governed by the rules of civil procedure in force in the Member State on the territory of which inspections and access shall be carried out. Courts of the Member State concerned shall have jurisdiction over complaints related to irregular conduct of enforcement. The amounts of the penalty payments shall be allocated to the general budget of the European Union.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {

          "reasoning": "article-Art35-Para9 -> article-Art35-Para6: Article 35(9)'s administrative character, civil enforcement and budget allocation apply only to the periodic penalty imposed under Article 35(6).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para9",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para6"
        }
      ],

          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "Recital 81's central concern is that periodic penalties against critical providers established in third countries remain enforceable; Article 35(9) is the exact operative paragraph declaring those payments enforceable and assigning civil-procedure and jurisdiction rules.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/recital-81",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para9"

        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "Penalty payments shall be of an administrative nature and shall be enforceable. Enforcement shall be governed by the rules of civil procedure in force in the Member State on the territory of which inspections and access shall be carried out. Courts of the Member State concerned shall have jurisdiction over complaints related to irregular conduct of enforcement. The amounts of the penalty payments shall be allocated to the general budget of the European Union.",
          "source_line_start": 7012,
          "source_line_end": 7012
        }
      ],
      "akn4eu_article_type_uri": "http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/resource-type/ART",

      "text_sha256": "8cb1bec69f753aef77a6238848f25021d9f1a98b107b0fa5a84c2047d069c941"
    },

    {
      "id": "article-Art35-Para11",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 35,
      "paragraph_number": "11",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
      "akn4eu_article_kind": "regular",
      "akn4eu_heading": "Powers of the Lead Overseer",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "Before imposing a periodic penalty payment under paragraph 6, the Lead Overseer shall give the representatives of the critical ICT third-party service provider subject to the proceedings the opportunity to be heard on the findings and shall base its decisions only on findings on which the critical ICT third-party service provider subject to the proceedings has had an opportunity to comment. The rights of the defence of the persons subject to the proceedings shall be fully respected in the proceedings. The critical ICT third-party service provider subject to the proceedings shall be entitled to have access to the file, subject to the legitimate interest of other persons in the protection of their business secrets. The right of access to the file shall not extend to confidential information or to the Lead Overseer’s internal preparatory documents.",
      "outbound_relations": [

          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art35-Para11 -> article-Art35-Para6: Article 35(11) conditions imposition of the Article 35(6) penalty on a hearing, defence rights and bounded file access.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para11",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para6"
        }
      ],

          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(i)",
          "text": "the conduct of an inspection in a third-country is deemed necessary by the Lead Overseer to allow it to fully and effectively perform its duties under this Regulation;",

          "marker": "(iii)",
          "text": "the critical ICT third-party service provider concerned consents to the conduct of an inspection in a third-country; and",

          "parent_marker": null,

          "source_line_end": 7095

        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(iv)",
          "text": "the relevant authority of the third-country concerned has been officially notified by the Lead Overseer and raised no objection thereto.",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,

      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "When oversight objectives cannot be attained by means of interacting with the subsidiary set up for the purpose of Article 31(12), or by exercising oversight activities on premises located in the Union, the Lead Overseer may exercise the powers, referred to in the following provisions, on any premises located in a third-country which is owned, or used in any way, for the purposes of providing services to Union financial entities, by a critical ICT third-party service provider, in connection with its business operations, functions or services, including any administrative, business or operational offices, premises, lands, buildings or other properties: (a) in Article 35(1), point (a); and (b) in Article 35(1), point (b), in accordance with Article 38(2), points (a), (b) and (d), and in Article 39(1) and (2), point (a). The powers referred to in the first subparagraph may be exercised subject to all of the following conditions: (i) the conduct of an inspection in a third-country is deemed necessary by the Lead Overseer to allow it to fully and effectively perform its duties under this Regulation; (ii) the inspection in a third-country is directly related to the provision of ICT services to financial entities in the Union; (iii) the critical ICT third-party service provider concerned consents to the conduct of an inspection in a third-country; and (iv) the relevant authority of the third-country concerned has been officially notified by the Lead Overseer and raised no objection thereto.",

      "akn4eu_sub_units": [
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(a)",
          "text": "the procedures for the coordination of oversight activities carried out under this Regulation and any analogous monitoring of ICT third-party risk in the financial sector exercised by the relevant authority of the third country concerned, including details for transmitting the agreement of the latter to allow the conduct, by the Lead Overseer and its designated team, of general investigations and on-site inspections as referred to in paragraph 1, first subparagraph, on the territory under its jurisdiction;",

          "text": "the mechanism for the transmission of any relevant information between EBA, ESMA or EIOPA and the relevant authority of the third country concerned, in particular in connection with information that may be requested by the Lead Overseer pursuant to Article 37;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(b)",

          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(c)",

          "marker": "(d)",
          "text": "the regular transmission of updates on regulatory or supervisory developments on the monitoring of ICT third-party risk of financial institutions in the third country concerned;",

          "depth": 1,

          "source_line_start": 7180,

      ],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "Without prejudice to the respective competences of the Union institutions and of Member States, for the purposes of paragraph 1, EBA, ESMA or EIOPA shall conclude administrative cooperation arrangements with the relevant authority of the third country in order to enable the smooth conduct of inspections in the third country concerned by the Lead Overseer and its designated team for its mission in that third country. Those cooperation arrangements shall not create legal obligations in respect of the Union and its Member States nor shall they prevent Member States and their competent authorities from concluding bilateral or multilateral arrangements with those third countries and their relevant authorities. Those cooperation arrangements shall specify at least the following elements: (a) the procedures for the coordination of oversight activities carried out under this Regulation and any analogous monitoring of ICT third-party risk in the financial sector exercised by the relevant authority of the third country concerned, including details for transmitting the agreement of the latter to allow the conduct, by the Lead Overseer and its designated team, of general investigations and on-site inspections as referred to in paragraph 1, first subparagraph, on the territory under its jurisdiction; (b) the mechanism for the transmission of any relevant information between EBA, ESMA or EIOPA and the relevant authority of the third country concerned, in particular in connection with information that may be requested by the Lead Overseer pursuant to Article 37; (c) the mechanisms for the prompt notification by the relevant authority of the third-country concerned to EBA, ESMA or EIOPA of cases where an ICT third-party service provider established in a third country and designated as critical in accordance with Article 31(1), point (a), is deemed to have infringed the requirements to which it is obliged to adhere pursuant to the applicable law of the third country concerned when providing services to financial institutions in that third country, as well as the remedies and penalties applied; (d) the regular transmission of updates on regulatory or supervisory developments on the monitoring of ICT third-party risk of financial institutions in the third country concerned; (e) the details for allowing, if needed, the participation of one representative of the relevant third-country authority in the inspections conducted by the Lead Overseer and the designated team.",

          "text": "exercise its powers under Article 35 on the basis of all facts and documents available to it;",

      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "When the Lead Overseer is not able to conduct oversight activities outside the Union, referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2, the Lead Overseer shall: (a) exercise its powers under Article 35 on the basis of all facts and documents available to it; (b) document and explain any consequence of its inability to conduct the envisaged oversight activities as referred to in this Article. The potential consequences referred to in point (b) of this paragraph shall be taken into consideration in the Lead Overseer’s recommendations issued pursuant to Article 35(1), point (d).",

    {
      "id": "article-Art37-Para1",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 37,

        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "The Lead Overseer may, by simple request or by decision, require critical ICT third-party service providers to provide all information that is necessary for the Lead Overseer to carry out its duties under this Regulation, including all relevant business or operational documents, contracts, policies, documentation, ICT security audit reports, ICT-related incident reports, as well as any information relating to parties to whom the critical ICT third-party service provider has outsourced operational functions or activities.",

          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art37-Para1"

          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art37-Para1"

      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [

          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "The Lead Overseer may, by simple request or by decision, require critical ICT third-party service providers to provide all information that is necessary for the Lead Overseer to carry out its duties under this Regulation, including all relevant business or operational documents, contracts, policies, documentation, ICT security audit reports, ICT-related incident reports, as well as any information relating to parties to whom the critical ICT third-party service provider has outsourced operational functions or activities.",

        {
          "type": "point",

          "text": "refer to this Article as the legal basis of the request;",

        {

          "text": "inform the representative of the critical ICT third-party service provider from whom the information is requested that he or she is not obliged to provide the information, but in the event of a voluntary reply to the request the information provided must not be incorrect or misleading.",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(e)",
          "source_line_start": 7294,
          "source_line_end": 7297
        }
      ],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "When sending a simple request for information under paragraph 1, the Lead Overseer shall: (a) refer to this Article as the legal basis of the request; (b) state the purpose of the request; (c) specify what information is required; (d) set a time limit within which the information is to be provided; (e) inform the representative of the critical ICT third-party service provider from whom the information is requested that he or she is not obliged to provide the information, but in the event of a voluntary reply to the request the information provided must not be incorrect or misleading.",

        }

          "text": "When sending a simple request for information under paragraph 1, the Lead Overseer shall:",

          "text": "indicate the right to appeal the decision to ESA’s Board of Appeal and to have the decision reviewed by the Court of Justice of the European Union (Court of Justice) in accordance with Articles 60 and 61 of Regulations (EU) No 1093/2010, (EU) No 1094/2010 and (EU) No 1095/2010.",

      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "When requiring by decision to supply information under paragraph 1, the Lead Overseer shall: (a) refer to this Article as the legal basis of the request; (b) state the purpose of the request; (c) specify what information is required; (d) set a time limit within which the information is to be provided; (e) indicate the periodic penalty payments provided for in Article 35(6) where the production of the required information is incomplete or when such information is not provided within the time limit referred to in point (d) of this paragraph; (f) indicate the right to appeal the decision to ESA’s Board of Appeal and to have the decision reviewed by the Court of Justice of the European Union (Court of Justice) in accordance with Articles 60 and 61 of Regulations (EU) No 1093/2010, (EU) No 1094/2010 and (EU) No 1095/2010.",

      "akn4eu_sub_units": [
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(a)",
          "text": "examine records, data, procedures and any other material relevant to the execution of its tasks, irrespective of the medium on which they are stored;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(a)",
          "source_line_start": 7413,
          "source_line_end": 7416
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(b)",
          "text": "take or obtain certified copies of, or extracts from, such records, data, documented procedures and any other material;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(b)",
          "source_line_start": 7427,
          "source_line_end": 7430
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(c)",
          "text": "summon representatives of the critical ICT third-party service provider for oral or written explanations on facts or documents relating to the subject matter and purpose of the investigation and to record the answers;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(c)",
          "source_line_start": 7441,
          "source_line_end": 7444
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(d)",
          "text": "interview any other natural or legal person who consents to be interviewed for the purpose of collecting information relating to the subject matter of an investigation;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(d)",
          "source_line_start": 7455,
          "source_line_end": 7458
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(e)",
          "text": "request records of telephone and data traffic.",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(e)",
          "source_line_start": 7469,
          "source_line_end": 7472
        }
      ],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "The Lead Overseer shall have the power to: (a) examine records, data, procedures and any other material relevant to the execution of its tasks, irrespective of the medium on which they are stored; (b) take or obtain certified copies of, or extracts from, such records, data, documented procedures and any other material; (c) summon representatives of the critical ICT third-party service provider for oral or written explanations on facts or documents relating to the subject matter and purpose of the investigation and to record the answers; (d) interview any other natural or legal person who consents to be interviewed for the purpose of collecting information relating to the subject matter of an investigation; (e) request records of telephone and data traffic.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art38-Para2__article-Art38-Para1__depends_on",
          "source": "article-Art38-Para2",
          "target": "article-Art38-Para1",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art38-Para2 -> article-Art38-Para1: Article 38(2)'s examination, copying, summoning, interviewing and traffic-record powers exist for the investigation authorised by Article 38(1).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art38-Para2",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art38-Para1"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art36-Para1__article-Art38-Para2__references",
          "source": "article-Art36-Para1",
          "target": "article-Art38-Para2",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "references",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art36-Para1 -> article-Art38-Para2: Article 36(1) selects the examination, copying and consensual-interview investigation powers in Article 38(2)(a), (b) and (d) for use outside the Union.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art36-Para1",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art38-Para2"
        },
        {
          "edge_id": "recital-88__article-Art38-Para2__provides_guidance_for",
          "source": "recital-88",
          "target": "article-Art38-Para2",
          "source_type": "recital",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "provides_guidance_for",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "Recital 88 explains why the Lead Overseer needs effective investigative powers; Article 38(2) supplies the specific record-review, copying, summons, interview and traffic-record powers used in those investigations.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/recital-88",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art38-Para2"
        }
      ],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [

          "text": "The Lead Overseer shall have the power to:",

          "source_line_end": 7406
        }

      "text_sha256": "cf07fb944e684b38907e9a3fa79b29222d117807e5470d0b7848717eadb8d19a"
    },
    {
      "id": "article-Art38-Para3",
      "type": "article_paragraph",

      "ancestry": [

      ],
      "text": "The officials and other persons authorised by the Lead Overseer for the purposes of the investigation referred to in paragraph 1 shall exercise their powers upon production of a written authorisation specifying the subject matter and purpose of the investigation. That authorisation shall also indicate the periodic penalty payments provided for in Article 35(6) where the production of the required records, data, documented procedures or any other material, or the answers to questions asked to representatives of the ICT third-party service provider are not provided or are incomplete.",
      "outbound_relations": [

          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para6"
        },

          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art38-Para3",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art38-Para1"
        }
      ],

    {
      "id": "article-Art38-Para4",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 38,
      "paragraph_number": "4",

      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "The representatives of the critical ICT third-party service providers are required to submit to the investigations on the basis of a decision of the Lead Overseer. The decision shall specify the subject matter and purpose of the investigation, the periodic penalty payments provided for in Article 35(6), the legal remedies available under Regulations (EU) No 1093/2010, (EU) No 1094/2010 and (EU) No 1095/2010, and the right to have the decision reviewed by the Court of Justice.",
      "outbound_relations": [

          "relation": "references",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art38-Para4 -> article-Art35-Para6: Article 38(4) requires the investigation decision to state the periodic penalty provided by Article 35(6).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art38-Para4",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para6"
        },

          "relation": "depends_on",

          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art38-Para4",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art38-Para1"
        }
      ],

      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "In order to carry out its duties under this Regulation, the Lead Overseer, assisted by the joint examination teams referred to in Article 40(1), may enter in, and conduct all necessary onsite inspections on, any business premises, land or property of the ICT third-party service providers, such as head offices, operation centres, secondary premises, as well as to conduct off-site inspections. For the purposes of exercising the powers referred to in the first subparagraph, the Lead Overseer shall consult the JON.",
      "outbound_relations": [

          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art39-Para1 -> article-Art34-Para1: the Lead Overseer's required JON consultation when exercising inspection powers depends on the JON created to coordinate oversight activities in Article 34(1).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para1",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art34-Para1"
        },

      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "In order to carry out its duties under this Regulation, the Lead Overseer, assisted by the joint examination teams referred to in Article 40(1), may enter in, and conduct all necessary onsite inspections on, any business premises, land or property of the ICT third-party service providers, such as head offices, operation centres, secondary premises, as well as to conduct off-site inspections.",
          "source_line_start": 7496,
          "source_line_end": 7496
        },
        {
          "sequence": 2,
          "text": "For the purposes of exercising the powers referred to in the first subparagraph, the Lead Overseer shall consult the JON.",
          "source_line_start": 7497,
          "source_line_end": 7497
        }
      ],
      "akn4eu_article_type_uri": "http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/resource-type/ART",

    },

      "akn4eu_heading": "Inspections",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(a)",
          "text": "enter any such business premises, land or property; and",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(a)",
          "source_line_start": 7507,
          "source_line_end": 7510
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(b)",
          "text": "seal any such business premises, books or records, for the period of, and to the extent necessary for, the inspection.",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(b)",
          "source_line_start": 7521,
          "source_line_end": 7524
        }
      ],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "The officials and other persons authorised by the Lead Overseer to conduct an on-site inspection shall have the power to: (a) enter any such business premises, land or property; and (b) seal any such business premises, books or records, for the period of, and to the extent necessary for, the inspection. The officials and other persons authorised by the Lead Overseer shall exercise their powers upon production of a written authorisation specifying the subject matter and the purpose of the inspection, and the periodic penalty payments provided for in Article 35(6) where the representatives of the critical ICT third-party service providers concerned do not submit to the inspection.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art39-Para2__article-Art35-Para6__references",

          "relation": "references",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art39-Para2 -> article-Art35-Para6: Article 39(2) requires inspection authorisation to state the Article 35(6) periodic penalty for failure to submit.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para2",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para6"
        },

          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para2",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para1"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [

          "text": "The officials and other persons authorised by the Lead Overseer to conduct an on-site inspection shall have the power to:",

      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "In good time before the start of the inspection, the Lead Overseer shall inform the competent authorities of the financial entities using that ICT third-party service provider.",

          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para3",

        }

      "inbound_relations": [],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [

          "text": "In good time before the start of the inspection, the Lead Overseer shall inform the competent authorities of the financial entities using that ICT third-party service provider.",

        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],

    {

      "type": "article_paragraph",

      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "Before any planned on-site inspection, the Lead Overseer shall give reasonable notice to the critical ICT third-party service providers, unless such notice is not possible due to an emergency or crisis situation, or if it would lead to a situation where the inspection or audit would no longer be effective.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art39-Para5__article-Art39-Para1__depends_on",
          "source": "article-Art39-Para5",
          "target": "article-Art39-Para1",

          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para5",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para1"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "Before any planned on-site inspection, the Lead Overseer shall give reasonable notice to the critical ICT third-party service providers, unless such notice is not possible due to an emergency or crisis situation, or if it would lead to a situation where the inspection or audit would no longer be effective.",
          "source_line_start": 7538,
          "source_line_end": 7538
        }

      "text_sha256": "fec4aaae13506e538a07b4060243efa8ab54becf959a48df2d9198b32ec45dc1"
    },
    {
      "id": "article-Art39-Para6",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 39,
      "paragraph_number": "6",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
      "akn4eu_article_kind": "regular",
      "akn4eu_heading": "Inspections",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "The critical ICT third-party service provider shall submit to on-site inspections ordered by decision of the Lead Overseer. The decision shall specify the subject matter and purpose of the inspection, fix the date on which the inspection shall begin and shall indicate the periodic penalty payments provided for in Article 35(6), the legal remedies available under Regulations (EU) No 1093/2010, (EU) No 1094/2010 and (EU) No 1095/2010, as well as the right to have the decision reviewed by the Court of Justice.",
      "outbound_relations": [

          "relation": "references",

          "reasoning": "article-Art39-Para6 -> article-Art35-Para6: Article 39(6) requires the inspection decision to indicate the periodic penalty available under Article 35(6).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para6",

        },

          "target": "article-Art39-Para1",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "article-Art39-Para6 -> article-Art39-Para1: Article 39(6) imposes submission and decision-content requirements when the onsite inspection authorised by Article 39(1) is formally ordered.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para6",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para1"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art39-Para7__article-Art39-Para6__depends_on",
          "source": "article-Art39-Para7",
          "target": "article-Art39-Para6",

          "confidence": "high",

        }

    {
      "id": "article-Art39-Para7",
      "type": "article_paragraph",

      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",

      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "Where the officials and other persons authorised by the Lead Overseer find that a critical ICT third-party service provider opposes an inspection ordered pursuant to this Article, the Lead Overseer shall inform the critical ICT third-party service provider of the consequences of such opposition, including the possibility for competent authorities of the relevant financial entities to require financial entities to terminate the contractual arrangements concluded with that critical ICT third-party service provider.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art39-Para7__article-Art39-Para6__depends_on",

          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para7",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art39-Para6"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [

          "text": "Where the officials and other persons authorised by the Lead Overseer find that a critical ICT third-party service provider opposes an inspection ordered pursuant to this Article, the Lead Overseer shall inform the critical ICT third-party service provider of the consequences of such opposition, including the possibility for competent authorities of the relevant financial entities to require financial entities to terminate the contractual arrangements concluded with that critical ICT third-party service provider.",
          "source_line_start": 7544,

          "text": "When conducting oversight activities, in particular general investigations or inspections, the Lead Overseer shall be assisted by a joint examination team established for each critical ICT third-party service provider.",

      "text": "The joint examination team referred to in paragraph 1 shall be composed of staff members from: (a) the ESAs; (b) the relevant competent authorities supervising the financial entities to which the critical ICT third-party service provider provides ICT services; (c) the national competent authority referred to in Article 32(4), point (e), on a voluntary basis; (d) one national competent authority from the Member State where the critical ICT third-party service provider is established, on a voluntary basis.       "text": "The ESAs shall, through the Joint Committee, develop draft regulatory technical standards to specify: (a) the information to be provided by an ICT third-party service provider in the application for a voluntary request to be designated as critical under Article 31(11); (b) the content, structure and format of the information to be submitted, disclosed or reported by the ICT third-party service providers pursuant to Article 35(1), including the template for providing information on subcontracting arrangements; (c) the criteria for determining the composition of the joint examination team ensuring a balanced participation of staff members from the ESAs and from the relevant competent authorities, their designation, tasks, and working arrangements.           "reasoning": "article-Art42-Para1 expressly makes the provider's endorsement notice or reasoned refusal a response to recommendations issued under article-Art35-Para1 point (d).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para1",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para1"

      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "Within 60 calendar days of the receipt of the recommendations issued by the Lead Overseer pursuant to Article 35(1), point (d), critical ICT third-party service providers shall either notify the Lead Overseer of their intention to follow the recommendations or provide a reasoned explanation for not following such recommendations.     },
    {

      "type": "article_paragraph",

      "akn4eu_heading": "Follow-up by competent authorities",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "The Lead Overseer shall publicly disclose where a critical ICT third-party service provider fails to notify the Lead Overseer in accordance with paragraph 1 or where the explanation provided by the critical ICT third-party service provider is not deemed sufficient. The information published shall disclose the identity of the critical ICT third-party service provider as well as information on the type and nature of the non-compliance. Such information shall be limited to what is relevant and proportionate for the purpose of ensuring public awareness, unless such publication would cause disproportionate damage to the parties involved or could seriously jeopardise the orderly functioning and integrity of financial markets or the stability of the whole or part of the financial system of the Union. The Lead Overseer shall notify the ICT third-party service provider of that public disclosure.",
      "outbound_relations": [

          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "The disclosure trigger in article-Art42-Para2 depends on article-Art42-Para1 because it arises only when the provider fails to give the intention or sufficient explanation required there.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para2",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para1"
        }

      "text": "Where a competent authority deems that a financial entity fails to take into account or to sufficiently address within its management of ICT third-party risk the specific risks identified in the recommendations, it shall notify the financial entity of the possibility of a decision being taken, within 60 calendar days of the receipt of such notification, pursuant to paragraph 6, in the absence of appropriate contractual arrangements aiming to address such risks.",

          "reasoning": "article-Art42-Para4 expressly warns that failure to fix contractual arrangements may lead to the suspension or termination decision authorised by article-Art42-Para6.",

      "text": "Upon receiving the reports referred to in Article 35(1), point (c), and prior to taking a decision as referred to in paragraph 6 of this Article, competent authorities may, on a voluntary basis, consult the competent authorities designated or established in accordance with Directive (EU) 2022/2555 responsible for the supervision of an essential or important entity subject to that Directive, which has been designated as a critical ICT third-party service provider.",

          "reasoning": "article-Art42-Para5 expressly begins upon receipt of the remedial-action reports that article-Art35-Para1 point (c) empowers the Lead Overseer to request.",

          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para1"
        },

          "relation": "references",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "The voluntary NIS2-authority consultation in article-Art42-Para5 is expressly positioned before a competent-authority decision under article-Art42-Para6.",

          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "The escalation to additional supervisory measures in recital-90 reaches its last-resort form in article-Art42-Para6, which authorises temporary suspension or termination of the relevant service use.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/recital-90",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para6"
        }
      ],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "Competent authorities may, as a measure of last resort, following the notification and, if appropriate, the consultation as set out in paragraph 4 and 5 of this Article, in accordance with Article 50, take a decision requiring financial entities to temporarily suspend, either in part or completely, the use or deployment of a service provided by the critical ICT third-party service provider until the risks identified in the recommendations addressed to critical ICT third-party service providers have been addressed. Where necessary, they may require financial entities to terminate, in part or completely, the relevant contractual arrangements concluded with the critical ICT third-party service providers.",
          "source_line_start": 7715,
          "source_line_end": 7715
        }
      ],
      "akn4eu_article_type_uri": "http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/resource-type/ART",
      "canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para6",
      "text_sha256": "e1b54ef5f6e5a18afe4a1211a303937454120fa78a859cf1d960b20ac9384df4"
    },
    {
      "id": "article-Art42-Para7",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 42,
      "paragraph_number": "7",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
      "akn4eu_article_kind": "regular",
      "akn4eu_heading": "Follow-up by competent authorities",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "Where a critical ICT third-party service provider refuses to endorse recommendations, based on a divergent approach from the one advised by the Lead Overseer, and such a divergent approach may adversely impact a large number of financial entities, or a significant part of the financial sector, and individual warnings issued by competent authorities have not resulted in consistent approaches mitigating the potential risk to financial stability, the Lead Overseer may, after consulting the Oversight Forum, issue non-binding and non-public opinions to competent authorities, in order to promote consistent and convergent supervisory follow-up measures, as appropriate.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art42-Para7__article-Art42-Para1__depends_on",
          "source": "article-Art42-Para7",
          "target": "article-Art42-Para1",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "The refusal-to-endorse scenario in article-Art42-Para7 depends on the provider response mechanism established by article-Art42-Para1 for accepting recommendations or explaining non-acceptance.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para7",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para1"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "Where a critical ICT third-party service provider refuses to endorse recommendations, based on a divergent approach from the one advised by the Lead Overseer, and such a divergent approach may adversely impact a large number of financial entities, or a significant part of the financial sector, and individual warnings issued by competent authorities have not resulted in consistent approaches mitigating the potential risk to financial stability, the Lead Overseer may, after consulting the Oversight Forum, issue non-binding and non-public opinions to competent authorities, in order to promote consistent and convergent supervisory follow-up measures, as appropriate.",
          "source_line_start": 7718,
          "source_line_end": 7718
        }
      ],
      "akn4eu_article_type_uri": "http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/resource-type/ART",
      "canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para7",
      "text_sha256": "415977df4ead08065cbad0ea17254989e95c5b13a0fc15c3b10680ec107154cd"
    },
    {
      "id": "article-Art42-Para8",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 42,
      "paragraph_number": "8",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
      "akn4eu_article_kind": "regular",
      "akn4eu_heading": "Follow-up by competent authorities",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(a)",
          "text": "the gravity and the duration of the non-compliance;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,

          "source_line_end": 7731
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(b)",
          "text": "whether the non-compliance has revealed serious weaknesses in the critical ICT third-party service provider’s procedures, management systems, risk management and internal controls;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(b)",
          "source_line_start": 7742,
          "source_line_end": 7745
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(c)",
          "text": "whether a financial crime was facilitated, occasioned or is otherwise attributable to the non-compliance;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(c)",
          "source_line_start": 7756,
          "source_line_end": 7759
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(d)",
          "text": "whether the non-compliance has been intentional or negligent;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(d)",
          "source_line_start": 7770,
          "source_line_end": 7773
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(e)",
          "text": "whether the suspension or termination of the contractual arrangements introduces a risk for continuity of the financial entity’s business operations notwithstanding the financial entity’s efforts to avoid disruption in the provision of its services;",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(e)",
          "source_line_start": 7784,
          "source_line_end": 7787
        },
        {
          "type": "point",
          "marker": "(f)",
          "text": "where applicable, the opinion of the competent authorities designated or established in accordance with Directive (EU) 2022/2555 responsible for the supervision of an essential or important entity subject to that Directive, which has been designated as a critical ICT third-party service provider, requested on a voluntary basis in accordance with paragraph 5 of this Article.",
          "depth": 1,
          "parent_marker": null,
          "path": "(f)",
          "source_line_start": 7798,
          "source_line_end": 7801
        }
      ],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "Upon receiving the reports referred to in Article 35(1), point (c), competent authorities, when taking a decision as referred to in paragraph 6 of this Article, shall take into account the type and magnitude of risk that is not addressed by the critical ICT third-party service provider, as well as the seriousness of the non-compliance, having regard to the following criteria: (a) the gravity and the duration of the non-compliance; (b) whether the non-compliance has revealed serious weaknesses in the critical ICT third-party service provider’s procedures, management systems, risk management and internal controls; (c) whether a financial crime was facilitated, occasioned or is otherwise attributable to the non-compliance; (d) whether the non-compliance has been intentional or negligent; (e) whether the suspension or termination of the contractual arrangements introduces a risk for continuity of the financial entity’s business operations notwithstanding the financial entity’s efforts to avoid disruption in the provision of its services; (f) where applicable, the opinion of the competent authorities designated or established in accordance with Directive (EU) 2022/2555 responsible for the supervision of an essential or important entity subject to that Directive, which has been designated as a critical ICT third-party service provider, requested on a voluntary basis in accordance with paragraph 5 of this Article. Competent authorities shall grant financial entities the necessary period of time to enable them to adjust the contractual arrangements with critical ICT third-party service providers in order to avoid detrimental effects on their digital operational resilience and to allow them to deploy exit strategies and transition plans as referred to in Article 28.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {

          "source": "article-Art42-Para8",
          "target": "article-Art28-Para8",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "references",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "The adjustment period in article-Art42-Para8 expressly protects deployment of the exit strategies and transition plans required by article-Art28-Para8.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para8",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art28-Para8"
        },
        {

          "source": "article-Art42-Para8",
          "target": "article-Art35-Para1",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "references",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "The risk and non-compliance assessment in article-Art42-Para8 expressly starts from remedial-action reports requested under article-Art35-Para1 point (c).",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para8",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art35-Para1"
        },
        {

          "source": "article-Art42-Para8",

          "relation": "references",

          "reasoning": "The NIS2 authority opinion considered under article-Art42-Para8 is expressly the voluntary opinion requested through article-Art42-Para5.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para8",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para5"
        },
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art42-Para8__article-Art42-Para6__references",
          "source": "article-Art42-Para8",
          "target": "article-Art42-Para6",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "references",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "Decision criteria enumerated by article-Art42-Para8 expressly govern the suspension or termination decision authorised in article-Art42-Para6.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para8",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para6"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "Upon receiving the reports referred to in Article 35(1), point (c), competent authorities, when taking a decision as referred to in paragraph 6 of this Article, shall take into account the type and magnitude of risk that is not addressed by the critical ICT third-party service provider, as well as the seriousness of the non-compliance, having regard to the following criteria:",
          "source_line_start": 7721,
          "source_line_end": 7721

        {

    {
      "id": "article-Art42-Para9",
      "type": "article_paragraph",

          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para9",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art32-Para4"
        },

    {
      "id": "article-Art42-Para10",
      "type": "article_paragraph",
      "article_number": 42,
      "paragraph_number": "10",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
      "akn4eu_article_kind": "regular",
      "akn4eu_heading": "Follow-up by competent authorities",
      "akn4eu_sub_units": [],
      "ancestry": [
        "CHAPTER V",
        "Section II"
      ],
      "text": "Competent authorities shall regularly inform the Lead Overseer on the approaches and measures taken in their supervisory tasks in relation to financial entities as well as on the contractual arrangements concluded by financial entities where critical ICT third-party service providers have not endorsed in part or entirely recommendations addressed to them by the Lead Overseer.",
      "outbound_relations": [
        {
          "edge_id": "article-Art42-Para10__article-Art42-Para1__depends_on",
          "source": "article-Art42-Para10",
          "target": "article-Art42-Para1",
          "source_type": "article_paragraph",
          "target_type": "article_paragraph",
          "relation": "depends_on",
          "confidence": "high",
          "reasoning": "The reporting duty in article-Art42-Para10 depends on the non-endorsement of recommendations that article-Art42-Para1 requires a critical provider to communicate and explain.",
          "source_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para10",
          "target_canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para1"
        }
      ],
      "inbound_relations": [],
      "akn4eu_source_paragraphs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "text": "Competent authorities shall regularly inform the Lead Overseer on the approaches and measures taken in their supervisory tasks in relation to financial entities as well as on the contractual arrangements concluded by financial entities where critical ICT third-party service providers have not endorsed in part or entirely recommendations addressed to them by the Lead Overseer.",
          "source_line_start": 7813,
          "source_line_end": 7813
        }
      ],
      "akn4eu_article_type_uri": "http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/resource-type/ART",
      "canonical_ref": "celex:32022R2554/article-Art42-Para10",
      "text_sha256": "1844b6a016c25f83670438bd7c6df330aea13b2cd75df27b14146aa8a085b269"
    },
    {
      "id": "article-Art42-Para11",
      "type": "article_paragraph",

      "paragraph_number": "11",
      "akn4eu_paragraph_kind": "numbered",
